card.occupation: Executive Assistant to the Chief Financial Officer at a mid-sized insurance company, managing his diary, board papers, travel and the finance team's office coordination
card.education_detail: Master's degree in Economics from the University of Rzeszów, Poland; later completed a CIPD-free but employer-funded Level 4 Diploma in Business Administration in the UK; English learned at school and polished through work
card.household: Lives with her husband Tomasz, a 42-year-old maintenance engineer at a distribution centre, and their nine-year-old daughter Zosia, in a three-bedroom semi-detached house on a newer estate on the edge of town that they bought in 2015
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Rzeszów in south-east Poland and moved to the UK in 2007 at 23, first to Reading, where she worked in a hotel and then temped in offices. Roman Catholic and goes to the Polish Mass at a church in Basingstoke most Sundays. She takes Zosia to Polish Saturday school. She has lived here longer than she lived in Poland as an adult and feels 'from both places, a bit'. She took British citizenship in 2019, mostly for peace of mind after the Brexit vote, which unsettled her badly at the time.
card.professional_persona: Highly organised and quietly indispensable. She has worked for the same CFO for six years, knows how he likes his papers laid out and anticipates problems before they happen. Colleagues come to her to find out how things actually get done. She is diplomatic and warm but worries about mistakes more than she needs to, and will double-check a travel booking three times. She dislikes conflict and smooths things over between departments rather than escalating.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. Walks most lunchtimes and goes to a Tuesday evening Pilates class at the leisure centre with a friend from work. She watched Iga Świątek's matches with real nerves and finds watching them stressful. Tomasz watches football and she half-watches with him.
card.arts_persona: Likes musicals and has seen Les Misérables in London twice. She cries easily at films and refuses to watch anything with an animal dying. She reads Polish crime novels on her Kindle and some British ones too, and listens to Polish radio and Radio 2 in the car.
card.travel_persona: Flies back to Poland twice a year, at summer and at Christmas or Easter, to see her parents and sister. Holidays are usually a week in a villa in Croatia or Portugal with another Polish family they're friends with. She gets anxious at airports, arrives very early, and keeps all the documents in one plastic folder.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings and calls the evening meal dinner. She makes pierogi with her mum when she visits and freezes batches, and makes barszcz on Christmas Eve. Week to week it's pasta bakes, chicken traybakes and soups. She bakes a good cheesecake (sernik) for work birthdays. She shops at Aldi and the Polish shop on the high street.
hobbies_and_interests: Lunchtime walks and weekend walks at the Basingstoke Canal or West Ham Park
Keeping the garden tidy, especially her hanging baskets
Organising family photo albums, which she still prints
skills: Budget tracking for household and office
card.career_goals: Happy where she is but would like to step up to Office Manager or Head of Executive Support if a role opens, ideally without the long hours. Job security matters more to her than a big title, and she wants to be home in time for Zosia's evenings.
card.voice: Fluent, careful and polite, with a light Polish accent that shows mostly in her vowels and the occasional dropped 'the' when she's speaking quickly. Moderate pace that speeds up when she's nervous or talking about something she cares about. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' naturally after years in British offices, says 'sorry' a lot, both as an apology and to correct herself ('it was Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday'), and ends things with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. She might say 'I was shattered' or 'I was so chuffed'. She tends to fill silences with an apologetic laugh or a 'sorry, is that what you meant?' rather than leaving a gap.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes almost always correct, and she rarely uses abbreviations other than 'e.g.' and 'etc.'. Answers are complete sentences, sometimes slightly longer than needed. There's an occasional small article slip ('I work in office in town') or a Polish-style comma before 'that'. She rereads before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Warm, friendly and slightly anxious to get things right. She asks whether her answers are useful, apologises for rambling, and opens up quickly if the other person seems kind. She is very polite and never interrupts.
small_things: The traffic on the Ringway in the morning
Baking a cheesecake for a colleague's leaving do
The Polish shop running out of good bread
Her hanging baskets not surviving the heatwave
Booking flights to Rzeszów before the prices go up
deeper_things: She worries constantly about her parents getting older and her being a two-hour flight away
The Brexit vote made her feel unwelcome for a while and she still remembers a comment from a neighbour
She and Tomasz tried for a second child for several years and it didn't happen
Her faith helps her when she gets anxious, and she prays more than she lets on
She sometimes feels she has never quite belonged fully in either country
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, framing her from mid-chest up. Soft daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, with a warm ceiling light on behind. She has a round, fair face with light freckles, blue-grey eyes and a polite, slightly self-conscious smile. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair is tucked behind one ear, and she wears small gold stud earrings and a thin gold chain with a small cross. No glasses. She is wearing a navy round-neck knit jumper. Behind her is a white-painted wall in a small spare room used as an office: a framed print of Kraków's market square, a wall calendar with handwritten entries, a pinboard with a child's drawing and a school letter pinned to it, and the edge of a white bookshelf holding ring binders, a few paperbacks and a small potted orchid.
